description: Network access, location, posture, endpoint profiling and device administration from Cisco ISE's logs. Passed and failed logins come from ISE's message class; sites come from the network devices' Location groups.
title: Cisco ISE Overview

definition.content:
**Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE)** decides which users and devices join the wired, wireless and VPN network, and authenticates administrators on network devices through TACACS+.

This dashboard shows ISE's logs: logins and failures, where they happen (site and network device), posture, the endpoints ISE profiles, and device administration.

- Filters only apply to the widgets whose events carry that field.

[Integration docs](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/cisco_ise/) · [Cisco ISE logs](/logs?query=source%3Acisco-ise) · [Cisco ISE syslog messages](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/security/ise/syslog/Cisco_ISE_Syslogs/m_SyslogsList.html)
Network logins and device administration at a glance.

definition.description: Network logins ISE accepted (message class `Passed-Authentication`; dACL downloads, `5232`, excluded). Includes ISE's re-authorizations after a Change of Authorization (`5236`). Network logins = RADIUS (802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass, wired and wireless), without TACACS+ admin logins.
definition.title: Passed logins

definition.description: Network logins ISE rejected (message class `Failed-Attempt`). Network logins = RADIUS (802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass, wired and wireless), without TACACS+ admin logins.
definition.title: Failed logins

definition.description: Failed network logins as a percentage of all network logins. Ignores the endpoint profile, authentication method and posture filters.
definition.title: Failure rate

definition.description: Distinct users with a passed network login, without MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), whose user name is the endpoint MAC address.
definition.title: Users

definition.description: Distinct endpoint MAC addresses with a passed network login.
definition.title: Endpoints

definition.description: TACACS+ logins to network devices that ISE rejected (`5401`).
definition.title: Failed admin logins

definition.content: Who logs in to the network, how, and why logins fail.

definition.description: Network logins over time: passed (`Passed-Authentication`) and failed (`Failed-Attempt`). Network logins = RADIUS (802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass, wired and wireless), without TACACS+ admin logins.
definition.title: Logins: passed vs failed

definition.description: Network logins by RADIUS flow type: wired or wireless, 802.1X or MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB).
definition.title: Access type

definition.description: Why ISE rejected network logins: ISE's failure reason code and text.
definition.title: Top failure reasons

definition.description: Network logins by authentication method: `Lookup` = MAB, `x509_PKI` = EAP-TLS (certificate), `MSCHAPV2` = PEAP (password), `PAP_ASCII` = PAP.
definition.title: Authentication methods

definition.description: Users with the most failed network logins. `INVALID` = a user name ISE does not know; MAB failures show the endpoint MAC address.
definition.title: Top failing users

definition.description: Endpoint MAC addresses with the most failed network logins.
definition.title: Top failing endpoints

definition.description: Endpoints ISE flagged for repeated failures, with the account: the most attempts one `5434` summary reported, and the number of `5449` notices (ISE now rejects the endpoint without logging each attempt).
definition.title: Repeated failures

definition.description: Endpoint MAC addresses with passed network logins, by number of distinct authentication methods, most first. Ignores the authentication method filter.
definition.title: Endpoints with several authentication methods

definition.description: Each failed network login with its user, endpoint, network device and failure reason.
definition.title: Failed login details

definition.content: Where logins happen: site and network device.

definition.description: Network logins by site (levels 1 and 2 of the network device's ISE Location group) and network device. N/A: the device has no Location group, or the event was split.
definition.title: Logins by site and network device

definition.description: Users with passed network logins, by number of distinct locations (ISE Location group) and network devices.
definition.title: Users in several locations

definition.description: Passed and failed network logins per network device (switch, wireless controller, VPN), most failures first.
definition.title: Network devices

definition.description: Failed network logins by site (level 2 of the Location group).
definition.title: Failed logins by site

definition.description: Wireless network logins by SSID. Wired logins have no SSID.
definition.title: Top SSIDs

definition.description: Passed network logins by the authorization profile ISE selected, with the VLAN, downloadable ACL and Security Group Tag it assigned (N/A when the profile sets none).
definition.title: Authorization results

definition.description: Which user and endpoint MAC address had each IP address, from RADIUS accounting (start, interim update, stop). Needs RADIUS accounting on the network devices.
definition.title: IP address to user and MAC

definition.content: Endpoint compliance when users log in.

definition.description: Passed network logins over time by posture status: `Compliant`, `NonCompliant`, `Pending`, `NotApplicable` (no posture policy matched). Needs ISE posture policies.
definition.title: Posture status

definition.description: Passed network logins that ISE assessed for posture, by posture status.
definition.title: Assessed logins by posture status

definition.description: Users and endpoints ISE let in although their posture was `NonCompliant`, with the authorization profile they got.
definition.title: Non-compliant endpoints granted access

definition.content: The endpoints ISE identifies on the network.

definition.description: Distinct endpoints ISE profiled or re-profiled in the time range (Profiler, `80002`).
definition.title: Endpoints profiled

definition.description: Distinct endpoints with a passed login whose profile is `Unknown`: ISE cannot tell what device they are.
definition.title: Unprofiled endpoints logging in

definition.description: Endpoints with a passed network login by the profile ISE matched, each MAC address counted once.
definition.title: Endpoints by profile

definition.description: Endpoints ISE profiled or re-profiled in the time range (Profiler, `80002`), by operating system. Needs ISE profiling probes that detect the OS.
definition.title: Endpoints by operating system

definition.description: Endpoints ISE profiled or re-profiled in the time range (Profiler, `80002`), by hardware vendor, from the MAC address prefix (OUI).
definition.title: Endpoints by vendor

definition.description: Endpoints with a passed login by endpoint identity group, each MAC address counted once.
definition.title: Endpoint identity groups

definition.description: Endpoints with an `Unknown` profile that logged in, with their user and network device.
definition.title: Unprofiled endpoints

definition.content: Administrators on network devices and changes to ISE itself.

definition.description: Administrators logging in to switches and routers through TACACS+: passed (`5201`) and failed (`5401`). Logins to ISE itself are in ISE admin logins.
definition.title: Admin logins on network devices

definition.description: Logins to ISE itself (web GUI and CLI) per administrator, passed and failed. Logins to network devices are in Admin logins on network devices.

search.query: source:cisco-ise @cisco_ise.message_code:(51000 OR 51004 OR 51005 OR 51006 OR 51007 OR 51008 OR 51020 OR 51021 OR 51022 OR 60081 OR 60082 OR 60185 OR 60186) $ise_node $user $client_ip

definition.title: ISE admin logins

definition.description: TACACS+ commands typed at privilege level 15 (`3300`), by administrator, command and network device.
definition.title: Privilege 15 commands

definition.description: TACACS+ commands ISE refused to authorize (`5402`), at any privilege level, by administrator, command and network device.
definition.title: Denied commands

definition.description: TACACS+ commands that change access or the device: `configure`, `username`, `enable`, `write`, `copy`, `reload`, `aaa`, `crypto`, `snmp-server`. Secrets are masked by the Datadog Agent. Clone the dashboard to change the list.

search.query: source:cisco-ise @cisco_ise.message_code:3300 @cisco_ise.tacacs.command_name:(configure OR username OR enable OR write OR copy OR reload OR aaa OR crypto OR snmp-server) $ise_node $site_level1 $site_level2 $site_level3 $network_device $user $client_ip

definition.title: Sensitive commands

definition.description: Changes to ISE's configuration (policies, rules, network devices) over time, without ISE's internal `DockerMetrics` messages.
definition.title: ISE configuration changes by admin

definition.description: Each ISE configuration change: administrator, action, object type and name, interface.
definition.title: ISE configuration change details

definition.description: Adaptive Network Control operations such as quarantine (`87751`), with the administrator, endpoint, operation and result, and Change of Authorization requests that failed (`5417`). Needs the Posture and Client Provisioning Audit and Failed Attempts Logging Categories.
definition.title: Quarantine and CoA details

definition.content: All Cisco ISE logs and setup problems.

definition.description: All Cisco ISE logs by status (ISE severity). Failed logins are `notice`, like passed ones.
definition.title: Logs by status

definition.description: Pieces of ISE events that ISE split into several logs, and logs whose syslog header didn't parse. Neither is parsed further.
definition.title: Split or unparsed events

definition.description: Logs by ISE Logging Category: shows which categories the ISE target sends.
definition.title: Logs by Logging Category

definition.description: Cisco ISE logs with status error or higher.

query.query_string: source:cisco-ise status:(error OR critical OR alert OR emergency) $ise_node

definition.title: Error logs
